I've been farming for two years now, so I'm still learning, but I've watched my neighbors closely and I know the basics of what works here in Quzhou. It's semi-arid, my well is reliable, and the soil is decent. I have 10.1 mu to work with and four crops to manage. My main system is eggplant — that's where I put the most land and attention because vegetables bring better income than grain. I keep wheat and maize partly out of habit and for home use and stability. Let me think through each crop.

**Wheat:** I'll put about 3 mu into winter wheat. It goes in October. I'll use an improved variety — the seed shop here sells Jimai 22 or similar, I know neighbors use it, I won't overthink it. I'll plough before sowing since I want a good seedbed. I'll irrigate four times: once at emergence if it's dry, at tillering, jointing, and heading. Two pesticide passes — one fungicide around jointing, one for aphids closer to heading. Fertilizer I'll base-dress with a compound and top-dress urea at jointing. I'm probably heavier on nitrogen than I need to be but that's what the neighbor does and I don't want to risk low yield.

**Maize:** After the wheat comes off in June, I rotate about 1.6 mu into summer maize. Hybrid seed, no question — everyone here plants hybrid maize. I'll do rotary tillage after wheat harvest. Three irrigations: before sowing, at tasseling, and grain fill. One pesticide pass for corn borer. Maize is low maintenance for me, it's more of a background crop.

**Eggplant:** This is my main crop — 3.5 mu. I start transplants in the greenhouse in late February and plant out in late March. Hybrid seed. The eggplant needs the most irrigation, I'll water about 8 times through the season. I'll apply pesticide 5 times — aphids, red spider mites, and Phytophthora blight are real problems here. I'll use rotary tillage and work in organic fertilizer base before planting. I put the most fertilizer here too, especially potassium since eggplant is heavy on it. Expected yield around 3,500 kg/mu — I got about 3,200 last year so I'm hoping to improve slightly.

**Chili:** 2 mu of chili, spring planting in April. I'll use an improved variety the local shop sells. Chili needs less water than eggplant but still quite a bit in the dry summer — 6 irrigations. Four pesticide passes. Rotary tillage before transplanting. I expect around 1,800 kg/mu fresh weight.
